# k3d-cluster

A k3d cluster on the operator's docker host.

<!-- Generated by nix/floe-docs.nix. Refresh: nix run .#refresh-docs -->

## Inputs

| input | type | default | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| auditLogging | submodule | `{}` | Recording what the API server was asked to do.  Here rather than on the cluster, because every field of it is a flag and a mount for an API server *this floe* creates — a managed control plane logs through its provider, and a cluster this lab did not make has no server to pass flags to. The cluster module used to hold it and reach into this variant through a per-provisioner hook to inject it.  |
| autoDeployManifests | list of (submodule) | `[]` | Manifests k3s applies at startup, before the node is Ready.  For the one case a floe cannot cover: something the cluster needs in order to finish starting. A CNI is the whole of that case today — a floe's bundles are applied to a cluster that is already up, so a floe providing the network would have to require the cluster that cannot start without it.  Anything that can wait for a running cluster belongs in a floe, where it gets ordering, readiness and drift handling. This gets none of those: k3s applies it once and nothing manages it afterwards, which is why `floes.cilium` also installs itself as an ordinary release.  |
| extraK3sArgs | list of (submodule) | `[]` | Flags handed to `k3s server` itself.  Distinct from the apiserver args, which reach only kube-apiserver: a cluster whose datastore is not its own embedded etcd says so with `--datastore-endpoint`, and that is a k3s flag, not an apiserver one.  Written last, after the disables and the CIDRs, so a lab that needs to override one of those can. k3s takes the last occurrence of a repeated flag.  Nothing validates the contents. A flag k3s does not know fails when the node starts, which is the only place that can be known.  |
| image | string | `"rancher/k3s:v1.31.4-k3s1"` | k3s node image. Pinned, not floating: a lab is reproducible or it is not. |
| instanceName | string | *(required)* | What k3d calls the cluster's containers. Distinct from `name` because two labs may each hold a cluster called `app` on one docker host, and the container names would collide.  |
| name | string | *(required)* | Cluster name, as members and the kubeconfig see it. Required. |
| network | null or string | `null` | Docker network the cluster's containers join.  Filled in by placement, like `instanceName`: which network a cluster shares is a fact about what else is on the host, and a floe is instantiated before it is placed. Null for a cluster created outside a lab, where k3d makes its own.  It was patched into the descriptor by the lab after the fact, through a per-provisioner hook keyed on `k3d` — which is the placement rule broken in code: the lab reached into one variant of a tagged union to set a field the floe had declared null.  |
| podSubnet | string | `"10.244.0.0/16"` | Pod CIDR. A decision, written down, not derived from the cluster's name: renaming a cluster would then silently move a running one's subnet.  |
| serviceSubnet | string | `"10.96.0.0/12"` | Service CIDR. Same reasoning as `podSubnet`. |
| version | string | `"1.31"` | Kubernetes minor version this cluster answers as. |
| wait | string | `"10m"` | How long to wait for the API server to answer once the cluster has been created.  Here rather than on the cluster, because how long a cluster takes to come up is a property of what makes it. The wait for an *apply* to settle belongs to whatever applies, and is `DELIVERY_POLICY`'s.  |

| alias | kind | what it carries |

## What it emits

Rendered by `every-floe` as the lab unit `core-claim`. A unit of the lab
installs nothing into a cluster, and its provisions are sealed inside the
lab's inclusion — so its declaration above is its interface.
